newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds rallied sharply as buyers chased scarce guilder paper to push benchmark 10-year yields to their lowest level for more than a month.
The yield on the January 2006 bond ended at 5.64 percent, compared with 5.75 percent on Friday.
"I saw good buying across the curve," said one London-based dealer, identifying interest in maturities between 2002 and 2004 and particular demand from Asian institutions.
"There's a shortage of (paper)," he added, echoing the views of traders through the day that few bond holders were willing to sell at current levels.
One trader said the 2002-2007 part of the yield curve performed well as 2002 and 2007 were the favoured maturities for a new bond issue to be announced on Friday.
A 2007 would replace the Jan 2006 as the 10-year benchmark but most players tipped a reopening of the September 2002 bond.
Another dealer said the Finance Ministry's Agent would find strong demand for the new issue as the government had been winding back supply in recent times.
"We need paper from the Dutch government very badly," he said.
